root_problem: Only historical and archived pilot evidence exists today, so the product-director-led standard chain still lacks a fresh from-scratch demand loop proving that the team can reuse it reliably.
business_goals: Create login-homepage-v2 as a fresh standard-chain demand, with canonical artifacts from Director through Delivery Owner.
Prove that each role has clear responsibility boundaries, low-noise outputs, and downstream-consumable handoffs.
Use the resulting evidence to judge whether one human plus an AI team can deliver a complete small feature through the standard process.
acceptance_criteria: Anonymous users who request the homepage are redirected to the login page.
The login page exposes username and password fields in a submit-ready form.
A valid configured credential creates a server-side session, sets an HttpOnly SameSite=Lax session cookie, and redirects to the homepage.
An invalid credential keeps the user on the login page, returns a readable error, and does not issue a session cookie.
Authenticated users can open the protected homepage and see their configured login identity, welcome content, and a logout action.
Logout expires the browser cookie, removes the server-side session, redirects to the login page, and prevents the old cookie from opening the homepage.
The fresh login-homepage-v2 evidence chain passes canonical validation without using old login-homepage-pilot completion evidence.
design_decisions: Use a new isolated Python standard-library HTTP example app so the pilot adds no unrelated product framework or dependency noise.
Load the configured login credential from environment variables or test-owned setup rather than hardcoding a business password.
Use server-side in-memory session state and an HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie for the local pilot journey.
Keep role-capability and noise-control evidence in login-homepage-v2 canonical artifacts instead of relying on historical pilot reports.
non_functional_requirements: Exercise the user journey through a real local HTTP server, not mocked request objects.
Keep new implementation and test files under the repository 400-line file limit.
Keep implementation isolated under examples/login_homepage_v2_app and tests/test_login_homepage_v2_app.py.
Return user-readable errors without exposing stack traces or internal exception details.
Use fresh proving commands for completion evidence and do not treat old login-homepage-pilot tests as this run's acceptance proof.
scope_boundaries: In scope: independent login-homepage-v2 evidence chain, single configured account login, protected homepage, logout invalidation, real HTTP acceptance tests, canonical validation, role-capability evidence, and noise-control evidence.

Out of scope: reusing old login-homepage-pilot completion evidence, registration, password reset, multi-user administration, role-based authorization, database persistence, production deployment, complex visual polish, business dashboards, analytics, and personalized homepage modules.

delivery_plan.goal: Deliver and validate the fresh login-homepage-v2 minimum login and protected homepage loop through the full standard chain.
